desert_p15_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_001.text: At the quarry on the second morning, the red mast looked smaller than the story Yue had carried home. Its cloth hook was empty. The municipal clinician's temporary sign had been removed from the shelter, and a worker used the cleared bench to mend a basket. The cask keeper recognized the party and asked why Han had sent fewer wheels. Gao explained the current route enquiry. He pointed east and said the old channel had run harder after the northern rain, although the quarry's own apron was dry. His travelling casks were all booked for local deliveries that week.

desert_p15_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_002.text: He had no surplus water for sale. Their planned stock remained their travelling stock. The repaired basket belonged to the quarry worker's wife. He had agreed to mend it on a quiet morning, and the quarry had obligingly produced a morning with no quiet at all. He asked Yue to hold the loose rim while he tightened the last binding. She did, standing clear of the cart path. He remembered the first rescue's boards and asked after the young guide's leg. Bao gave only the general news that treatment continued in town.

desert_p15_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_003.text: The worker nodded and returned to the basket, pleased enough by a living patient's future to stop demanding a conclusion. His wife would still want the basket finished before noon. The keeper gave them a note from the guides' transport account, now settled against the municipal contractor rather than the rescued men's field wages. Yue had not expected to see that small administrative knot untied. Bao read the public settlement line and asked where the contractor kept its clinical transfer record. The keeper supplied the town clinic reference, not the patients' private details.

desert_p15_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_004.text: Du asked whether any local workers had used the east approach recently. A woman carrying a repaired wheel rim answered from behind him: she had walked as far as the split boulder yesterday and seen water below the outer shelf. She had not crossed the narrowing. The cask keeper's daughter had copied every cancelled loan receipt into a little schoolbook for practice. She showed Yue the page recording the two ninety-litre casks. The letters were careful and the first number had been written backward, then corrected. Yue praised the correction more than the tidy column.

desert_p15_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_005.text: The girl asked whether accountants travelled as far as surveyors. Du said some accountants travelled farther, though they took their columns with them. Her father said she could travel after she stopped borrowing his ink without replacing the lid. She replaced it immediately and asked Du whether map offices employed people who could count. He advised her to learn to question counts as well.

desert_p15_006.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p15_006.text: Show me where you stood on this sketch. The split boulder appears in two accounts, but this turn may be farther south than either person meant. There, you approached from the quarry path. And the water was below the shelf, not running over it. Thank you. I will enter your observation with yesterday's date and the limit of your walk. We will inspect beyond it ourselves. Did you hear anyone there, or see a cart? No? That is useful too, provided I do not let it become a claim that nobody lives farther east.

desert_p15_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_007.text: The woman with the wheel rim took Gao's pencil and marked her exact standing place. She held the pencil like a tool she did not trust, pressing hard enough to nearly break the tip. Gao gave her a board beneath the page. The woman said she made axle washers, not pictures. Gao answered that the marked place was a better picture than a graceful wrong line. That pleased her. She had been interviewed by a subscriber's runner before, who wanted a short yes or no about the road. She had refused both because she had seen only the footpath.

desert_p15_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_008.text: Now she could point at the limit and have it survive the conversation. The woman laughed at the last sentence. Her cousin traded in Onion Hollow and had always complained that quarry people thought the east stopped at their wall. She described a willow with a crooked trunk beside the village well and warned the party that the older well keeper hated being called an ancient custodian. He was merely old and tired of carrying everybody's buckets. Yue liked him before meeting him. The mason asked about the stone shelf.

desert_p15_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_009.text: The woman said it held walkers, not quarry wagons, and the cart route rose above it. She showed them where the two lines separated. The day acquired a practical shape beneath the names. A quarry boy led the mules past the loading yard while the drivers inspected the east turn. One animal nosed his pocket and discovered an apple he had intended to eat himself. The boy held it higher, protested, then divided it with the help of the first driver. He gave both leading mules a piece and retained the largest for his own breakfast.

desert_p15_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_010.text: The municipal driver asked why his pair had been left out. The boy said they looked like animals with regular employment and therefore less deserving. The driver considered the judgement and bought another apple. The distinction between private and municipal animals dissolved into crunching. They stopped by the foreman's office for the current diversion gate setting. The berm remained in service at its limited discharge, with an inspection ordered downstream after the collective's complaint. The deputy had already measured the first junction; the valley enquiry would fill the receiving section.

desert_p15_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_011.text: Gao copied the setting and the day's observed level, then checked the outlet from the public observation point. The reading belonged to that hour. A worker asked whether she intended to close the gate. She said the party had no such authority and would report conditions to the route officer. He looked relieved, then told her which foreman could actually order a local change if an urgent message arrived. The foreman had been called to the receiving enquiry and expected a reprimand. He was visibly relieved when Gao first asked for a reading rather than a confession.

desert_p15_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_012.text: Then she asked whether the downstream households had been notified before the flow changed, and his relief vanished. He had sent the instruction through the old district office address. The office had stamped receipt; the household notice was not in his file. The route officer would need to follow the message chain. The foreman offered the stamped copy without destroying it or blaming a clerk by name. Yue thought the paper looked much too small to carry the distance it had failed to travel.

desert_p15_013.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p15_013.text: I will attach that copy with the date. The downstream enquiry can establish where it stopped. For the current setting, I need the actual opening and the observed level at this point. If the valley residents have not received a notice, we will tell them what we know when we arrive. That still leaves the office's duty to issue it properly. Our field message is an immediate account, not a repair to the missing chain. Please give us the urgent return contact for a changed condition.

desert_p15_014.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p15_014.text: A road to the right foreman is more useful today than an argument about the wrong clerk.

desert_p15_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_015.text: Beyond the quarry, the east cart route rose over bare limestone. Its pale ledges looked like stair treads cut for a person too large to use the road. The municipal driver kept his pair slow through the first turn and let the other cart remain back until his wheels cleared. Yue walked the short outside line with the mason, collecting loose flags after Gao's observations. Tuo watched from her permitted seat. She recognized the rock fin above the bend but not the new scrape where a recent small slide had shed gravel.

desert_p15_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_016.text: The driver stopped while the mason inspected that scrape. It was shallow and stable; they cleared its loose stones before passing. The east track's first rise drew breath from the mules in long audible pulls. The drivers rested them on the broad level shoulder before the narrow turn. Yue gave the municipal driver his water vessel and moved aside as he checked the inside trace. The conservator asked whether she could help by holding the outer animal. He said her best help was to leave it room and keep the dry box still.

desert_p15_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_017.text: She accepted the answer cheerfully, settling the box against its strap. It was one of several ways expertise travelled: a person knowing when to give instruction, another knowing when not to improve it. The conservator carried her umbrella outside the cart cover to shade the instrument case while Gao made the level check. Du said an umbrella beside a desert road looked like a declaration against weather. She said weather had won too many declarations already. A gust turned the umbrella slightly inside out. The repaired spoke held. She looked vindicated, and Yue admired the spoke more than the argument.

desert_p15_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_018.text: Below them, the old channel first appeared as a grey ribbon between low walls. Water moved through part of it, catching the sun in disconnected flashes. The natural valley and the old construction did not yet explain how their flow joined. Tuo pointed to three low stone heaps above the bend. They had once marked a track toward a winter shelter. Only two appeared on Du's later sheet. He explained that the third had been omitted as redundant. The nephew's recent description placed a garden path near the third heap, making it useful again for a different purpose.

desert_p15_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_019.text: Gao did not restore the old route merely because a marker survived. She placed the heaps as visible references and left the path for current observation. Tuo tapped the third drawn heap with her fingernail. She said it was gratifying to see a neglected stone find employment after so many years. At the split boulder, Gao separated the party's two observations. The current water passed below the shelf on the lower side. The cart track remained above it, dry on firm rock, with a turn narrow enough to require a halt before each vehicle.

desert_p15_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_020.text: A small branch in the flow led under a drift of gravel toward the historical gate identifier. Du checked the carved mark from the safe upper path using the field glass issued with Gao's equipment. It matched the copied letter's first gate code. He wanted to climb closer. The mason pointed to an unsupported edge and saved them both the trouble of arguing. Du stayed where the code could already be read. The municipal driver had never seen an old gate code cut into rock. He expected lettering and was disappointed by its simple bar-and-notch form.

desert_p15_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_021.text: Du demonstrated the code's relation to the copied inventory without touching the unstable edge. The driver said the quarry used similar marks for barrow loads and asked whether the same workers might have made both. Du said the pattern was common in several districts, which made it a reference rather than a signature. The driver liked that answer. It spared the expedition another palace, and it meant a man could understand part of a long-dead work site without knowing the name of every person who had built it. Yue found a child's sandal on the high path beyond the turn.

desert_p15_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_022.text: It was old enough that its leather had stiffened, with a willow twig threaded through the broken fastening. She left it where it lay after noting the location. It did not prove a current missing child. Around the next shoulder, a recent line of onion skins hung from a low branch above a household garden. Those skins were a better sign of present work. Tuo laughed when she saw them. She had spent years remembering the village's false spring blossoms and still enjoyed being deceived by them. The drivers could see actual roofs beyond the garden now.

desert_p15_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_023.text: At the old sandal, Yue remembered the shoemaker's girl testing her knot. She could see why a rush fastening might last just long enough for a child to reach home. The conservator crouched on the firm path to look without taking the sandal up. Its leather and twig were evidence of some past passage, but their dry weathering did not give her a dependable date. Yue left a little drawing in the notebook rather than a dramatic description. When Du asked what she had found, she showed him the ordinary fastening. He studied it longer than the gate code.

desert_p15_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_024.text: Things people repaired for themselves could be less tidy and more intimate than things an office had marked. Onion Hollow stood along a shallow upper bench, its eleven occupied household compounds divided by walls of local stone. Smoke rose from two cooking sheds. A boy crossed between them carrying a pail nearly too large for his arms; an older woman relieved him of it before he could spill. The party stopped outside the first compound rather than drive between the walls. Gao gave the route enquiry reference to a resident who had come to inspect the carts.

desert_p15_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_025.text: He read slowly, tracing the district number with a rough finger. Then he pointed uphill to the well court. The well keeper would be there, and the household representatives would hear the same account together. The first resident who met them wore a belt of knotted cord and had a small onion tucked into it. He removed the onion while reading the scope, apparently to keep it from pressing against his ribs. The second driver could not stop looking at it.

desert_p15_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_026.text: When asked, the man said his wife had given it to him to take to the kitchen and he had been interrupted by carts. The driver pointed to the nearby cooking shed. The resident sighed, admitted defeat and passed the onion through its doorway before guiding them uphill. Yue hoped the district officer might someday put as much clear direction into a document. The crooked willow was unmistakable. Its trunk bent away from the well as if the tree had overheard something it disliked below. The older keeper stood beneath it with a rope loop in one hand.

desert_p15_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_027.text: When Du began his polite introduction with keeper of this ancient source, the man interrupted before ancient could spread. He said his name was on the annual service board and his age was none of the office's business. Du tried again with well keeper and succeeded. Yue could see the latest lining repair recorded on a small slate beside the parapet. The previous year's petition had not vanished entirely into the district number. The well keeper's service board had a corner repaired with a metal strip.

desert_p15_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_028.text: He explained that a visitor had once leaned a wet bucket against it until the wood split. Since then, every visiting party had been watched around the buckets. Du stepped back from the parapet without being asked. Gao kept the field case on a dry stone away from the rope sweep. The keeper noticed both acts. His manner remained sharp, but the sharpness changed from exclusion to ordinary impatience. He asked whether the party had a proper rope measure or would simply stare into the shaft like the last district runner.

desert_p15_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_029.text: Gao produced the issued measure and asked where he preferred her to stand. Gao explained the new flow and the receiving enquiry. The keeper took them to a high viewpoint within the court, from which the lower channel could be seen running north of the houses. Their well stood above that level in a lined shaft, usually covered against grit. The new surface water had not entered it so far as the keeper's morning inspection showed. That did not settle every source question.

desert_p15_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_030.text: Bao asked for the community's ordinary service records and offered a current field screening with the keeper present. He agreed after asking whether the result would be his too. She said he would receive the same dated account the expedition received. The lining descended beneath the parapet in pale rings. Cool air came up when the keeper lifted the cover, carrying the mineral smell of enclosed stone rather than the surface channel's wet silt. He lowered his ordinary draw carefully.

desert_p15_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_031.text: Bao took the fresh sample from that draw with the controls prepared, leaving the bucket and rope in the keeper's usual order. Yue watched a dark moth move along the shaded inside rim. The keeper warned her not to touch it; not because it was sacred, but because it might be the only moth in Onion Hollow clever enough to avoid his wife's lamp. She let it retain that advantage. The household representatives were two women and a younger man, chosen locally for this month's common work. They sat on overturned clean baskets beside the willow.

desert_p15_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_032.text: One woman wanted the quarry flow reduced before it reached the lower gardens. The man wanted the channel kept because it could water a planted strip that had been dry for years. The second woman asked whether anyone had measured the old spill throat downstream. Neither had. Gao described the proposed inspection and asked for a resident who knew the present foot route. The well keeper offered his nephew, who maintained the lower garden wall. He did not offer the whole community's trust along with the nephew's afternoon.

desert_p15_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_033.text: The younger representative wanted the new channel to revive his grandmother's lower garden. He spoke of old rows as if they were waiting plants rather than stone-bounded earth. The woman beside him had lost a goat in the last flood season and wanted every new stream far from the houses. Both had good reasons and incomplete pictures. Gao asked them to show the garden and the goat's crossing on the same sketch. Their marks lay on different sides of the spill throat. The argument grew quieter once the difference was visible. It did not disappear.

desert_p15_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_034.text: They still needed to know how much water the narrowing would receive in a northern storm.

desert_p15_035.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p15_035.text: I crossed the outer track once in winter and once before a market many years ago. Your paths have changed since then. I can compare the older turns and show why the office trace confused us, but I will follow a person who knows today's ground. My ankle also keeps me off long broken slopes on this journey. If that makes me less magnificent than the town promised, tell the town I survived the loss. I would rather come to your well as a useful guest than arrive at the relay store as a difficult patient.

desert_p15_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_036.text: Tuo recognized the younger man's grandmother's household name from her winter visit. He asked whether she remembered the woman herself. Tuo remembered a lamp, a bowl of hot onion soup, and a voice telling her not to put wet boots beneath the bed. The man laughed and said the boot rule remained law in that house. His grandmother was gone, but his mother enforced it with equal authority. Tuo did not try to turn the remembered soup into ownership of his family. She thanked him for the news and asked which winter path his mother still used.

desert_p15_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_037.text: An old kindness could open a conversation without closing it around the past. The younger representative smiled at Tuo and asked whether the onion-skin flowers had fooled her on her first visit. She admitted it. He said they had fooled his uncle every spring until the children stopped counting. The conversation softened the meeting without resolving its water dispute. Yue helped move the baskets so Gao could lay her sketch on a flat stone. The well keeper's nephew arrived carrying a mason's line and a small hoe. He had repaired the lower wall after the last seasonal rain.

desert_p15_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_038.text: He described the old relay as a roofless outer court with a partly sheltered inner room. Nobody in the village used it as a house. The nephew carried his mason's line in a tin with a dent shaped almost exactly like a heel. The village girl said he had stepped on it himself. He blamed a wall stone and she said the stone had worn his boots. The visiting mason examined the line, found it serviceable and let the family dispute continue. Gao asked the nephew to accompany the channel inspection for paid local guiding time under the district rate.

desert_p15_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_039.text: He accepted after checking when he would be back to help with the evening gate. There was always a second task in a place people actually inhabited. The paid guide's day had to leave room for it. Bao examined a fresh well sample with the keeper, using the purchased field sets and controls. The tested draw fell within the kit's relevant mineral and hazard limits, with ordinary appearance and no field indication requiring an immediate stop. That was a dated screen, not a guarantee against tomorrow's changed channel.

desert_p15_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_040.text: The community already strained and boiled its drinking supply under its own routine. The expedition bought no water from the well; its tanks remained sufficient for the planned circuit. Bao gave the keeper the result and asked him to tell her promptly if surface water approached the lining or the draw changed. He placed the slip inside the service box, beside the old petition. Bao compared the sample's field appearance with the blank and the appropriate reference checks. The keeper watched her hands closely, distrustful of colour changes he had not learned to read.

desert_p15_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_041.text: She explained each test in ordinary terms and gave him the recorded result rather than merely tell him to relax. He asked whether a good result meant his rope could remain frayed another month. She said the kit had expressed no opinion about rope. He grinned. The household representatives laughed, and the keeper promised to replace the worst section before the week's end. Health was becoming a subject he could argue with rather than an outsider's verdict over his court. The court also contained two covered service cisterns, each holding two hundred litres.

desert_p15_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_042.text: Their glazed interiors had been cleaned after the lining repair, lids seated on sound rims, taps working above the dirt splash. A hundred litres of the community's own treated reserve was divided between them that day, leaving three hundred of actual free capacity. The keeper showed the marks because the enquiry concerned emergency supply as well as flow. Those cisterns belonged to the households, not the caravan. Yue wrote the capacities beside the keeper's account. At that moment they looked like reassuring spare space, a quiet part of the court beneath the willow's divided shade.

desert_p15_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_043.text: The two cistern lids had different handles because one had been replaced by a local potter. The keeper showed the sealed glazing around both outlet fittings and the dated cleaning line on his board. The visiting mason examined the stands from the public court and found no current rocking or undermined foot. Bao confirmed that the cleaning and covered treatment storage were part of the community's routine. They were useful emergency vessels precisely because people had maintained them before an emergency.

desert_p15_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_044.text: Yue sketched the different handles so that later capacity accounts could not merge the two into a grander single reservoir. The keeper said he liked a drawing that admitted his repairs were ugly. A girl came from a cooking shed with a bowl of chopped onions and asked whether the visitors wanted supper or only more numbers. The representatives said the party would use its own provisions, though guests were welcome to buy vegetables. The girl negotiated a price with the first driver and returned with enough onions to perfume their camp.

desert_p15_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_045.text: Du asked whether the festival skins were saved from ordinary cooking. She stared at him, then asked where else skins might be obtained. Yue rescued him by asking how the flowers were tied. The girl showed her two quick knots and declined to explain them a third time. She had work, and strangers were slow. The onion girl had a chipped blue bowl she used for prices. She put pebbles into it while counting the vegetables, then removed one because the visiting driver had been pleasant. He told her to keep the agreed price.

desert_p15_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_046.text: She put the pebble back and asked whether town people always negotiated upward. He said only when they had been fairly treated and were hungry. She approved of hungry as an explanation. Du bought two small onion-skin flowers from her craft basket, one for his apprentice and one for no named recipient. Yue watched him choose the second carefully. She suspected the umbrella's owner might acquire it by the end of the journey. The proposed relay approach lay east of the village beyond the old spill throat.

desert_p15_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_047.text: The nephew drew a small bridge that had carried local walkers over the shallow cut during dry weather. It was not a cart bridge. The cart route stayed on the upper bench to a turning shoulder, from which the store could be approached by foot. Gao and the mason would inspect that shoulder and the first stable access in daylight. Du could join them from approved positions with the conservator, while Bao remained near the village until a site treatment corner was chosen. Yue would carry the light survey flags and support boards.

desert_p15_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_048.text: Tuo would help compare route marks from the firm upper ground. The mason went over the foot-route diagram with the nephew using four loose stones. The largest represented the relay's outer retaining shoulder. The little footbridge crossed a shallow current below it and reached the high garden strip on the opposite side. The old spill throat lay downstream of both. Carts could reach the stable upper turning place but could never use the footbridge. Yue moved one stone to make the relation clearer. The nephew thanked her and corrected its angle. Du copied the corrected arrangement immediately.

desert_p15_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_049.text: The inventory's narrow opening remained on the relay side; nobody had yet seen whether it led to a safe room or simply let wind through a broken wall. Three residents were working on a high garden strip beyond the footbridge: the keeper's older sister and two younger wall workers. They had taken their own food and water that morning and expected to return by the local path before dark. The nephew could see their bright cloth from the viewpoint and called across; a figure answered with a raised hoe.

desert_p15_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_050.text: It was a commonplace exchange between people used to different sides of a cut. Gao marked their working place as occupied on the current sketch. The old municipal trace had left it blank. The blank had contained onions, a repaired wall, and three people lifting their arms in ordinary greeting. The older sister called from the high strip to ask whether anyone in the camp had ginger. Du looked startled, as though his purchase for Tuo had developed a second purpose without permission. Tuo produced the packet and asked what the sister offered in exchange.

desert_p15_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_051.text: She held up a bunch of fresh herbs. The nephew carried a small portion across after the mason confirmed the presently stable foot line. Both women approved of the trade and left most of the ginger with Tuo. Yue watched the nephew's crossing. The bridge's dry boards and low current gave no reason to imagine tomorrow's danger, but she drew them while they were still ordinary. The party camped on a firm communal shoulder offered by the household representatives for the agreed two inspection nights. The ground lay above the visible channel and outside private gardens.

desert_p15_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_052.text: The drivers checked the turn and kept both carts ready to leave toward the quarry. Tuo's foot was examined after the day's seated travel; there was mild stiffness but no renewed swelling. Bao limited the evening walk anyway. Du wanted to visit the relay at once, while the light was still good. The conservator said late light was no substitute for the mason's access assessment. He looked toward the east and accepted the night he had been given. The camp shoulder's offer came with one condition: the household path to the well must stay clear.

desert_p15_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_053.text: The second driver marked the cart wheel line far enough back that no traveller had to brush against a tethered mule. The animals settled better there than on the exposed ridge. Children appeared at the shoulder's edge and were directed toward the open side, away from harness and hooves. One asked the conservator what lived in her box. She answered paper supports. He thought she meant birds. She opened the empty upper compartment to show him the boards, then closed it before the dust could join them. He departed in search of more interesting luggage.

desert_p15_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_054.text: The older keeper visited camp carrying a maintenance board. He wanted it included in any description of the well, because published reports often made household labour look like a source's natural generosity. The board listed lining checks, rope replacements, cleaning and the families contributing each season. Gao copied its public entries with permission. The keeper asked whether her route office would pay for a spare rope. She said the commission did not cover gifts disguised as assessment, but she could carry his request with its actual cost. He nodded, more satisfied by the plain answer than by Du's ancient compliment.

desert_p15_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_055.text: He had been negotiating with offices long enough to prefer a named purse. The well keeper's maintenance board recorded a dispute from two seasons earlier, when a family had paid in labour instead of coin. Du asked whether that private detail belonged in the public copy. The keeper considered and covered the line with his hand. The public report could state that households maintained the source collectively; it did not need to distribute old quarrels to paying map buyers. Gao copied the capacity and service dates without the family's contribution. The keeper seemed pleased that someone had asked.

desert_p15_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_056.text: He had shown the board to establish work, not to invite a distant room to decide which neighbour had been generous enough. Yue took the bread cloth down to the village girl for a stronger knot in its corner. The girl inspected the household mark and asked whether Yue had children. She said no. The girl said she had two younger brothers, which was worse for cloth. One brother appeared almost on command, trying to carry a bowl with both hands and one elbow.

desert_p15_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_057.text: The girl took it from him, scolded him, and set a portion aside that he plainly liked. Yue asked whether the family had always lived here. Their grandmother had, the girl said; her mother had spent several years in town and returned when the well work needed hands. People could leave a place without ceasing to belong to it. The girl's younger brother wanted to know whether Yue's sword had cut a giant serpent. She said it had mostly travelled in its sheath lately. He asked whether that disappointed the sword. She admitted she had never asked it.

desert_p15_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_058.text: The girl said tools preferred work they survived. Her brother found this unbearably sensible and went to practise serpent noises behind the cooking shed. Yue helped the girl wash the chopping board using her own household water, directed into the garden's ordinary reuse vessel. They discussed town shoe prices while the serpent hissed in the background. The girl's next ambition was a pair of boots that did not require apology after every rain. In the evening Gao and the nephew inspected the first portion of the upper cart route.

desert_p15_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_059.text: The mason tapped the outer edge and checked the supporting stone where the track narrowed. It was presently sound within the cart loads they brought, but the lower cut had begun eating loose material below one approach. He marked a monitoring point and asked the household representatives to keep foot traffic away from the raw lip. The route's safe margin depended on the visible shelf remaining as assessed. Gao recorded the current state and the signs that would require withdrawal. Yue could hear water below, hidden from the track by a fold of rock.

desert_p15_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_060.text: On the monitored approach, a loose pebble rolled down the raw lip and stopped in a crack. The mason watched it rather than follow it with his body. He asked the nephew whether the lip had looked the same last week. It had been wider, the nephew said, perhaps by a hand, though he had not measured it. Gao established a fresh visible reference from firm ground, dated and drawn from two measured reference positions. They would check it the next morning and withdraw if the approach changed beyond the assessed margin. Tuo disliked the narrow shelf on sight.

desert_p15_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_061.text: The mason said dislike was useful if it made people look, less useful if it pretended to be a load rating. They returned before the garden workers. The three figures were still visible on the high strip, preparing their own return. The older sister wore a yellow headcloth; a young man carried the repaired wall's unused stakes. Tuo watched them cross the little footbridge one at a time, each taking the familiar line without fuss. The nephew met them at the village end and took the stakes. There was no accident, no warning withheld by fate.

desert_p15_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_062.text: They would go back the next morning if the ground stayed fit. Yue liked seeing the day's occupied mark become three living neighbours walking home. It made the map feel less like a collection of places where somebody might later need rescue. The three returning gardeners stopped at camp to inspect the visitors. The older sister's yellow cloth had acquired a green stain from the herb bundle. One younger worker carried a repaired hoe and asked the municipal driver about town metal courses. The driver told him the current enrolment deadline and the fee his brother had been saving.

desert_p15_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_063.text: The worker could not afford that term, but wanted the details anyway. He borrowed Yue's pencil to write them on a scrap. A neighbour's practical ambition joined the driver's family ambition without requiring either man to promise the other's future. The scrap went into the worker's dry waist pouch, beside his garden receipts. The other young worker was the older woman's niece. She asked Bao whether an old shoulder pain ought to be treated as an injury if it hurt only after lifting stones.

desert_p15_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_064.text: Bao said pain after a specific load was still worth describing, then asked the woman privately about timing and movement. She offered a brief low-load assessment and advised against the provoking lift until a fuller visit could be arranged. The niece agreed reluctantly because the wall mattered to her aunt. Bao spoke to the aunt as well, without disclosing anything the niece did not permit. The wall would need lighter work or another pair of hands. It could not acquire a healed shoulder by being important. Supper smelled strongly of the purchased onions.

desert_p15_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_065.text: The driver had chopped them too coarsely, which the village girl discovered when she passed the camp and expressed with merciless accuracy. He offered her the knife. She improved two remaining onions in half the time and demanded a taste of the result. Bao made room for her at the edge of the meal, using the visitor's own cup and the paid vegetables rather than pretending their water account had gained another permanent adult. The girl said town travellers cooked as if every piece of food might escape. The conservator replied that some of the lentils had already tried.

desert_p15_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_066.text: Du wisely confined himself to eating. The village girl tasted the lentils, declared them improved and asked whether the mason always looked so solemn. He said the solemnity kept loose stones from making assumptions. She laughed harder than the joke required, relieved to discover the oldest stranger had a joke at all. The first driver offered her a clean spoon to take home. She refused because it was expedition gear and she had plenty of spoons. Yue offered one of her purchased spare paper sheets instead for the flower prices. The girl accepted that readily. Different gifts carried different weight.

desert_p15_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_067.text: The sheet was folded into her apron before the boy could turn it into a serpent.

desert_p15_068.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p15_068.text: I spoke with the household representatives about the well after the screen. They want a source officer to review the lining if the new channel remains active. That is sensible. The current slip is useful for today's draw; it should not be framed and forgotten while the ground changes beneath it. The clinic supplier gave me enough sets for this inspection and contingencies, but not an endless testing season. I will save the remaining controls for actual questions. If anyone sees a changed draw, tell the keeper and me. Meanwhile eat your onions.

desert_p15_069.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p15_069.text: We have spent enough of the day making good supper wait for another sentence.

desert_p15_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_070.text: Bao checked Tuo's ankle under the camp shade while the others cleaned the meal vessels. Tuo reported stiffness honestly and wanted to know whether the next day's outer viewpoint required more walking than she had agreed. Gao consulted the nephew and kept her role at the high turn; Yue could carry the reference notes back and forth. Tuo disliked being reduced to a voice at a turn. Bao reminded her that half the party wanted that voice. The guide rolled her eyes, then smiled.

desert_p15_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_071.text: She could be useful without spending every last improvement in her foot on a performance nobody had asked to see. The water entries closed at ten hundred and fifty-seven litres after one hundred and twenty-three actually used. Five hundred and twenty-nine remained in the first tank and five hundred and twenty-eight in the second, including their protected compartments. The fuel stock stood at thirty-two kilograms after another four used for the day's camp work. No village water had been added to the caravan.

desert_p15_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_072.text: The household cisterns retained their own hundred litres and three hundred litres of free space, a separate account. Gao checked the figures with both drivers while Bao wrote the day's medical and source notes. Yue finished washing the common spoons before the evening chill reached the shoulder. Gao checked the water count twice because the uneven tank division irritated her. One litre separated the two remaining stocks, a harmless consequence of actual vessel draws. Du suggested dividing it with a ceremonially important cup. She told him to take the next washing water from the fuller tank and cease being helpful.

desert_p15_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_073.text: Yue wrote the present figures without making them symmetrical. The protected threads stayed uncut. The source result belonged in a different column because nothing from the well had entered either cart. When they finished, Gao leaned back against the field case and admitted that she was tired of her own pencil. Du lent her his for tomorrow, as a practical joke she chose to accept. Du set the copied valley inventory beneath a stone weight and tried to line its descriptions up with the nephew's account. A relay court, a receiving niche, a shuttered inner repository.

desert_p15_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_074.text: One sketch showed a long narrow opening high in the wall. The nephew knew an opening that whistled in north wind, but had never measured its length. He said the building had no hidden underground city, only old retaining work and a room most children were told to leave alone. Du looked relieved and faintly disappointed. The conservator pointed out that a roofless room could hold enough difficulty without a city beneath it. He agreed, slower than he should have. The inventory described the relay court as sheltered for sorting.

desert_p15_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_075.text: The nephew said the local gardeners still used its outside wall for shade, which made the old phrase suddenly physical. He did not know of records in the inner room; its shutter had been stiff since his childhood. The conservator asked whether anyone forced it for storage. He said no. Onion sacks went to the outer niche and were removed after the harvest. This spared her one kind of damage while suggesting another: a room closed for years might hold dust, insects and failing paper without anyone intending harm.

desert_p15_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_076.text: She checked the box clasp as though the old room could hear it. Yue walked back to the well court before sleep to return the girl's knife. The older sister with the yellow headcloth was there, emptying her garden basket. She asked whether the party would be near the store tomorrow. Yue said only where the mason cleared access. The woman nodded and said the inner wall kept shade late into the morning, useful when one had to sort bulbs. She had used the outer court as a work shelter, never the paper room.

desert_p15_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_077.text: They stood beneath the crooked willow while the last light left the channel. The woman picked a dry onion skin from Yue's cloak and tied it into a tiny flower. No claim accompanied the gift. The older sister asked Yue what she liked best about town. Yue thought of the clinic, the instrument shop, the rented room's washing line, and finally said hot buns available before anyone asked her to plan a meal. The woman laughed and said she preferred town shoes. Then she looked at her own patched soles and admitted she disliked town noise.

desert_p15_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_078.text: They agreed that wanting one thing from a place did not oblige a person to want all of it. The sister gathered her basket. Her niece called from the path, carrying the hoe on the painless side. They went home together while Yue carried the tiny flower toward camp. Night gathered from the valley floor upward. The upper shoulder stayed light longer, then became a dark line carrying nine bedrolls, two carts and four quiet animals. Tuo's plain ankle cloth hung by her seat; her brother's bordered piece lay folded inside her coat. Du finally put the inventory away.

desert_p15_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_079.text: Across the hollow a household door opened briefly, spilling warm square light onto a stone path. Yue watched someone carry a covered pot inside before the door closed. Tomorrow's relay store was already in her mind, but the place beside it would not let itself disappear. It had onions, a disliked compliment, a willow, and people who expected their well to remain useful after visitors went home. At the last common watch, Gao and Yue could see three channel reflections between folds of rock. They did not yet know the flow at the old spill throat.

desert_p15_080.speaker: narrator
desert_p15_080.text: Northward, clouds banked over the distant hills without covering the local stars. Gao entered their presence as weather observation, not a prophecy. She wanted the channel inspected early next morning and the route margin rechecked before the party approached the relay. Yue agreed, then listened to a household singing somewhere below the willow. The tune had four falling notes and a pause for breath. It sounded like a song someone would still sing if no survey ever reached this valley. That was a useful way to hear it.
